Write a short blog post about the habit of saving money. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the post only.
final_message:
Let me say a word to you today about the habit of saving money. I do not believe there is any lesson that a young man or a young woman can learn that will be of more lasting service than this one. It is not a question of how much you earn. It is a question of what you do with what you earn.

I have known people who received very small wages, and yet, by being careful and regular, they laid something by every week. I have known others who received a great deal more, and yet, at the end of the year, they had nothing to show for it. The difference was not in the money. The difference was in the habit.

Now, a habit of this kind is not formed in a day. You must begin, and you must begin in a small way. Do not wait until you have a large sum to put aside. If you can save a nickel today, save it. If you can save a dime tomorrow, save that also. In time you will find that the nickels and the dimes have grown into dollars, and that the dollars have grown into something upon which you can stand. "Take care of the pennies," as the old saying goes, "and the dollars will take care of themselves."

I want you to see, too, that saving money is not merely a matter of having something in the bank. It is a matter of character. The person who has learned to say "no" to a foolish expense has learned to govern himself. The person who has learned to wait, and to deny himself a present pleasure for the sake of a future good, has gained a kind of strength which the world respects, and which it always will respect. Such a person is not easily frightened when hard times come, because he has made ready for them.

Some will say that it is a small matter, and that it is not worth the trouble. I answer that there is nothing small about it. Nearly every man who has made a place for himself in the world will tell you that he began by learning to save. He did not do it because it was pleasant. He did it because he saw that it was right, and because he saw that it would lead to independence.

Let us, then, make up our minds today that we are going to begin. Let us look carefully at our expenses, and let us ask ourselves, in each case, whether the money is being used wisely. If we do this faithfully, and if we keep at it year after year, the time will come when we shall be glad that we started, and when others will be glad to follow our example.
